outcome: A face-down permanent has only the characteristics the allowing ability lists, such as 2/2 with no name, text, subtypes or mana cost.
A permanent turned face down by an effect listing no characteristics becomes a 2/2 nameless creature with no text, subtypes or mana cost.
An effect that turns an already face-down permanent face down changes nothing.
A permanent put onto the battlefield face down does not trigger its enters-the-battlefield abilities.
A spell cast face down is evaluated with only face-down characteristics for effects and casting prohibitions.
The permanent controller may turn a face-down permanent face up only when the allowing ability or rules permit; spells normally cannot be turned face up.
A permanent turned face up regains its normal characteristics, keeps effects already applied to it and does not trigger enters-the-battlefield abilities.
A face-down permanent that becomes a copy keeps the face-down characteristics and takes the copied values when turned face up.
An "as turned face up" ability applies while the permanent is being turned face up, not afterwards.
Revealing a face-down permanent reads its characteristics ignoring continuous effects.
